essentials.title: Lead your department meeting
essentials.description: Work through the core agenda: previous actions, coverage, student learning, assessment and moderation, teaching practice, resources and safety, upcoming milestones. Close each item with an owner and a due date, and meet more often around assessments and exams.
essentials.timing_text: At least every two weeks — tick it in the weeks you meet

source.quote: Departments meet at least every two weeks, with minutes and named actions

essentials.title: Meet the Principal to review your department
essentials.description: Bring department performance, implementation progress, support needs and the actions you agreed last time. Keep the follow-up written down with named owners.
essentials.timing_text: Every two weeks — tick it in the weeks you meet

source.quote: Principal - HOD meeting: every two weeks for department performance, implementation, support needs, and agreed actions.

essentials.title: Carry out your share of formal classroom observations
essentials.description: You are one of the school's appraisers, so your observations count towards each teacher's F2 score. Record each one in Edunav Appraisal and hold the Glow / Grow / Go conversation straight after the lesson. Never formally observe a teacher you have mentored.
essentials.timing_text: Throughout each semester, following the observation split you agreed

source.quote: The Subject Leader / Head of Department, Principal, or Academic / Cambridge Coordinator formally observes you at least three times per semester

essentials.title: Do short walkthroughs and give written feedback
essentials.description: Walkthroughs are developmental: no score, and never part of F2. Use the Walkthrough Form and share your feedback with the teacher in writing through Edunav.

source.quote: These visits may occur anytime and should include written feedback on the designated Walkthrough Form.

essentials.title: Look over the homework calendar for your subject
essentials.description: Check the shared Edunav homework calendar so students do not get too many core-subject assignments on the same day, and talk to the teachers concerned when deadlines pile up.
essentials.timing_text: Weekly (the Assessment Policy gives this as its example)

source.quote: with the SL/Academic Coordinator reviewing weekly to ensure no more than 2 core-subject assignments land on the same day

tasks.title: Check every course has a current Scheme of Work and map
tasks.description: Each map links units to Cambridge objectives and national outcomes, with planned teaching weeks and room for revision. Make sure the department also has a current coverage tracker.
tasks.timing_text: July — start of the academic year

source.quote: Confirm timetable, staffing, schemes of work, external dates, and curriculum maps.

tasks.title: Bring your Department Handbook up to date
tasks.description: Check roles, current references, meeting rhythm, action tracking and links to live evidence. Remove any superseded assessment term, old appraisal rule or local weighting; the handbook implements network rules, it never rewrites them.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the year (and whenever a syllabus or network rule changes)

source.quote: Review at the start of the year, at Semester I close, and when a syllabus or network rule changes.

tasks.title: Agree objectives with each teacher you appraise
tasks.description: Share all the evidence before the meeting, review last year's objectives, then agree new ones with success criteria, including classroom observation. Keep an accurate record and review progress in interim discussions through the year.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the academic year

source.quote: Future objectives linked to the job role, experience, school priorities, teacher standards, and future career progression

tasks.title: Agree who observes whom this semester
tasks.description: Agree the observation split with the Academic Coordinator and the Principal, so every teacher in the appraisal population is covered and nobody is observed five times. Teachers still in induction are not on the F2 schedule.
tasks.timing_text: Start of each semester

source.quote: agree at the start of each semester how the required observations are shared between you, the Principal, and the Subject Leaders

tasks.title: Hold growth-focus conversations with the teachers you support
tasks.description: In July agree one, at most two, growth areas per teacher. In December read progress together (Still Working On It / Getting There / Now Consistent), in January set the next focus, and close with a full review at year end. Teachers in induction stay in the induction pathway.
tasks.timing_text: July, end of Semester I, January and end of the year

source.quote: Kickoff conversation: agree on the focus area together, using the Step 2 diagnosis as a starting point, not a verdict handed down

tasks.title: Hold a short coaching touch with each teacher you support
tasks.description: Pick one strategy from the Teacher Toolkit for the agreed focus and one sign to notice. After a week or two of trying it, let the teacher reflect first, then decide together whether to keep, adapt or replace it.
tasks.timing_text: Once in each half of the year: October and April (suggested placement)

source.quote: try it for 1–2 weeks, then discuss whether to keep, adapt, or replace it

tasks.title: Take part in the Assessment Committee
tasks.description: With the Academic Coordinator, the Principal and the other Heads of Department, review assessment data and student outcomes, and agree improvements to assessment practice and teacher support.
tasks.timing_text: August, November and February (the June annual review falls after the teaching weeks)

source.quote: The Committee is chaired by the Academic Coordinator (AC) and comprises the School Principal, all Heads of Department (HoDs)

tasks.title: Review your department's curriculum coverage tracker
tasks.description: Mark each unit On Track, Watch, At Risk or Escalated. An At Risk unit needs a written recovery action and owner; never solve it by silently dropping required Cambridge content.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: once a month

source.quote: Curriculum-coverage review and recovery actions; assessment and feedback timeliness/quality patterns; student-performance tracking with targeted support

tasks.title: Run a department moderation meeting
tasks.description: Review sample student work together and check that teachers of the same subject apply the rubrics and mark schemes in the same way. Use Cambridge exemplar material for IGCSE and A Level.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: at least once a semester (the policy says "regular")

source.quote: Departments conduct regular moderation meetings to discuss marking standards

tasks.title: Check teachers have the resources to teach the plan
tasks.description: Look at availability, condition, access, replacement needs, storage and safe use, not only the inventory list. Science departments follow the Science & Laboratory Handbook for laboratory requirements.
tasks.timing_text: Once a semester (suggested: early in the semester)

source.quote: At least once per semester, review whether teachers have the materials needed to deliver the planned curriculum well.

tasks.title: Hold the inter-level department meeting
tasks.description: Meet colleagues teaching your subject at other levels to check curriculum continuity and transition between grade bands, and to share resources.
tasks.timing_text: Quarterly (suggested placement)

source.quote: Inter-level department meetings: quarterly for curriculum continuity, transition, resource sharing, and cross-level collaboration.

tasks.title: Get your department ready for the Synchronized Test
tasks.description: Check every class has covered the semester's chapters, agree how structured answers will be marked against the mark scheme, and plan remedial follow-up and the Edunav entries before the reports.
tasks.timing_text: Two weeks before EASE Week 2 (7–11 Dec 2026) and EASE Week 4 (10–14 May 2027)

source.quote: Upcoming Teacher-Paced / Synchronized responsibilities, marking consistency, feedback quality, and remedial follow-up.

tasks.title: Record the Semester I close-out in the Department Handbook
tasks.description: Note coverage completed and carry-forward gaps, lessons from assessment and moderation, student-support actions, useful practices, resource needs and one to three Semester II priorities.
tasks.timing_text: At Semester I close

source.quote: major coverage completed and any carry-forward gaps;

tasks.title: Turn the year's review into next year's priorities
tasks.description: Use the Semester I close-out and this semester's evidence to choose a few department priorities for next year, not a long wish list.
tasks.timing_text: Year end (shown in the last teaching week)

source.quote: At year-end, convert these into a small number of next-year priorities rather than a long wish list.

tasks.title: Make sure your share of formal observations is complete
tasks.description: Without the minimum number of valid observations a teacher's F2 stays incomplete. Plan any missing ones now, avoiding the last day before a holiday and exam dates.
tasks.timing_text: A few weeks before each semester ends

source.quote: If the required minimum number of formal observations has not been completed, F2 remains incomplete

tasks.title: Hold End-of-Year Conferences for the teachers you appraise
tasks.description: The conference brings in the year's F2 observations and adds F3, scored only after the teacher has presented their evidence. Share all evidence beforehand and write the appraisal statement afterwards.
tasks.timing_text: Later in Semester II

source.quote: Gather and review appropriate evidence and ensure that all evidence has been shared with the appraisee prior to the meeting

tasks.title: Read your subject's Cambridge results and plan follow-up
tasks.description: Look at grade distributions, components and predicted versus actual grades with your teachers, and agree what changes in teaching and support. Results stay confidential.
tasks.applies_when: Your subject has Cambridge IGCSE, AS or A Level candidates
tasks.timing_text: After results release: May/June results early-to-mid August; Oct/Nov results mid-January

source.quote: Heads of Department receive subject-level reports; the leadership team reviews the whole-school picture

tasks.title: Spot-check the marking of the Progression Test
tasks.description: Check a sample of the teachers' marking against the Cambridge mark scheme, then make sure the analysis leads to re-teaching. For Stage 9, it should lead to a short Checkpoint intervention plan.
tasks.applies_when: Your department teaches Lower Secondary English, English as a Second Language, Mathematics or Science
tasks.timing_text: After each Progression Test is marked (suggested placement: Stage 8, Stage 7, Stage 9)

source.quote: The Head of Department or Subject Leader should complete a simple spot-check of marking to support consistency.

tasks.title: Plan EASE Academic reading into department meetings
tasks.description: Work through the Tier 1 resources together in meeting time rather than leaving teachers to do it alone. Individual EASE Academic scores stay confidential to each teacher.
tasks.applies_when: Your department teaches English, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology or Integrated Science
tasks.timing_text: About 8 weeks before each EASE Academic date (5 Dec 2026, 15 May 2027)

source.quote: Departments are encouraged to work through Tier 1 collaboratively during department meeting time rather than individually.

tasks.title: Agree your department's portfolio evidence plan
tasks.description: Agree which normal pieces of work students may select, about 1–2 per subject per semester. Use existing work before creating any portfolio-only task; the portfolio is never graded.
tasks.applies_when: Your school runs the Grade 7–12 student portfolio
tasks.timing_text: Early in each semester (suggested placement)

source.quote: As a default reference, departments may plan approximately 1–2 purposeful pieces of evidence per subject per semester

tasks.title: Hold your weekly mentor session
tasks.description: Use the standard structure: check-in, review last week's action, preview next week, one curriculum or pedagogy topic, and one or two actions with an owner and date. A group workshop does not replace it.
tasks.applies_when: You are a certified mentor with an active mentee
tasks.timing_text: Every week (30 minutes in Semester 2; monthly in Semester 3)

source.quote: Standard rhythm: weekly one-hour mentor session plus the Observation Spine and agreed practice tasks.

tasks.title: Observe your mentee and debrief the same day
tasks.description: Write low-inference evidence, hold a 10–15 minute debrief that starts with the mentee's own reflection, and agree one Glow, one Grow and one Go. Write it up within 7 days; it never enters appraisal.
tasks.applies_when: You are a certified mentor with a first-year mentee
tasks.timing_text: Once a month, August to March (Months 2–9)

source.quote: Stage 2 is on track when weekly mentoring is happening, early plans show increased independence, monthly observations and debriefs are current

tasks.title: Map your mentee's 8-touch cycle for Semester 2
tasks.description: Plan the two co-teaches, four mentor observations and two peer observations as one schedule, so no formal observation is duplicated just to satisfy two labels.
tasks.applies_when: You are a certified mentor with a first-year mentee
tasks.timing_text: Start of Semester 2

source.quote: At the beginning of Semester 2, map all eight touches against the school calendar and the Month 7–9 observation requirements.

tasks.title: Attend the mentor Calibration Session
tasks.description: All active mentors score the same anonymised sample observation and compare results, so the Emerging → Extending scale means the same thing in every school.
tasks.applies_when: You are a certified mentor with an active mentee
tasks.timing_text: Once per semester, on the date Eduversal sets (suggested placement)

source.quote: all active mentors attend a Calibration Session once per semester (90 minutes, online)

tasks.title: Walk your successor through the Department Handbook
tasks.description: Update the handbook first, then cover the open items in the meeting action tracker, carry-forward coverage gaps and student-support actions in progress. If you cannot, the Academic Coordinator gives the briefing.
tasks.applies_when: You are handing over the Subject Leader role
tasks.timing_text: When the Subject Leader changes (shown at year end)

source.quote: When the Subject Leader changes, the outgoing leader updates this handbook and walks the new leader through it.

notes_for_reviewer: v1 problems found (subject-leader.json v1.1): (1) the same 40-week arc, so the Synchronized Test leadership sat at W14/W33, moderation at W16/W37 and the End-of-Year Conferences at W39 — after the real last teaching week (7 May 2027); (2) a 'compliance' priority on about 15 tasks and Indonesian regulatory anchors that no live document uses; (3) weekly tasks the live documents do not ask for: a weekly 'coaching touch' (the Capacity-Building Guide has two short touches a semester plus two conversations) and weekly sampling of department lesson plans (the School Principals Checklist gives plan review to the Principal's meeting with Subject Leaders); (4) other roles' duties: matching new teachers with mentors (the Principal assigns) and recommending candidates' subjects and tiers for entries (Exams Officer process; Principal / AC approve); (5) a duplicate id (SL-W25-001 appears twice) and citations to documents that are not in the school-facing export (Lesson Planning Guide & Template 26-27).

New optional field `applies_when` is used on 9 of 25 tasks (Cambridge results, Progression Tests, EASE Academic subjects, portfolio, mentoring, handover). The seeder and the Teachers Hub page need to support it.

Subject Leaders also teach. This file holds only the Subject Leader duties; their own teaching and appraisal tasks (F1 records, Student Survey action plan, F3 + F3L evidence for their own End-of-Year Conference, EASE Academic, Teacher-Paced Test time slots) are in teachers.json. Please decide whether the Teachers Hub shows both lists to a user who holds both sub-roles, or whether a few teacher tasks should be copied here.

Priority choices to check: SL2-008 and SL2-021 are 'core' because the Teacher Appraisal Handbook §2.3 is titled 'Appraiser (Head of Department)' and lists these duties (the AC file marks its End-of-Year Conference task 'recommended' because the handbook does not say which appraiser runs the conference). SL2-010/011 (capacity building) are 'core' because the guide's rhythm table names 'Subject Leader / HoD' as the lead, although the guide calls itself a 'School Support Resource' — downgrade to 'recommended' if you read it as guidance. Department Handbook tasks (SL2-007, 018, 019) are 'recommended' because the template says 'Recommended owner'; the handover (SL2-030) is 'core' because that sentence is directive. SL2-004 (walkthroughs) and SL2-005 (homework calendar) are 'recommended' because the sources say 'may' and 'for example'.

Two biweekly meetings (department meeting, Principal–HOD meeting) are essentials with timing_text 'every two weeks', because the `when` schema has no biweekly type; the Principal file does the same for its side of the HOD meeting (SP2-006).

SL2-009 (who observes whom) quotes Induction Module: Academic Coordinators 26-27, which is addressed to the AC but names the Subject Leaders as the other party to the agreement (and §3.4 says 'In most schools the Subject Leader or Head of Department carries a share of the classroom observations'). Same duty as AC2-008, seen from the Subject Leader's side.

Assessment Committee (SL2-012): the Assessment Policy §14.3 adds a June 2027 annual review (with Eduversal) after the teaching weeks; the AC file shows it in the last teaching week, this file leaves it out to keep that week light. Make the two files consistent.

Placements without a live date (said so in timing_text): inter-level meetings 'quarterly' (24 Aug, 9 Nov, 15 Feb, 19 Apr), moderation 'regular' (mid-semester), coverage tracker (monthly, matching AC2-027), coaching touches in the guide's 'Term 2' and 'Term 4' (12 Oct, 12 Apr — the guide's Term 1–4 are quarters of the school year; I kept the word 'Term' out of the task text to avoid confusion with the retired EASE term windows), Progression Test spot-checks (5 Oct, 18 Jan, 22 Mar — one week after the teacher file's administration weeks), EASE Academic reading (about 8 weeks before each date, per the Preparation Resources timeline), Cambridge results (17 Aug, 18 Jan — the Exams Officer Handbook release windows, matching the Principal's SP2-031).

Title drift to confirm against Drive: the Capacity-Building Guide is 'Teacher Development: Capacity-Building Guide 26-27' by its export file name, but its body and sibling documents call it 'Teacher Capacity-Building Guide 26-27' and once 'Teacher Appraisal: Capacity-Building Guide 26-27'. 'Career Growth: Framework 26-27' is used as instructed (the document's own control block says 'Eduversal Career Growth Framework').

Not added, to keep the list light or because no live text gives it to the Subject Leader: Mentor Certification before mentoring (a precondition, not a dated task — NN3; the Principal assigns mentors), Cambridge syllabus-update and predicted-grade reviews (School Principals Checklist gives both to the Principal 'with subject coordinators / subject leaders'), the Grade Committee (optional network role), and subject counselling (the counselling guide gives readiness advice to subject teachers and the decision to the AC / Counsellor; it is in teachers.json as ST2-022).

Load, simulated over 36 teaching weeks with my own reading of the `when` rules: a typical Subject Leader (no applies_when tasks) has 0–3 dated tasks a week plus 5 essentials; the heaviest weeks are 13 Jul 2026 and 3 May 2027 (3 each). With every applies_when task switched on (mentor + Cambridge + Lower Secondary + portfolio + EASE Academic + handover) the peak is 5 (weeks of 3 Aug and 5 Oct 2026, and 3 May 2027). Please re-run with the real seeder.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: Review a rotating sample of department lesson plans for quality and coherence, not length.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: F1.4 judges plan quality, yet no live document gives the Subject Leader a regular look at plans between observations; the Principals Checklist gives plan review to the Principal's meeting with Subject Leaders.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Teaching & Learning: Lesson Planning Guide & Template 26-27

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: Recommend each Cambridge candidate's subject and tier (e.g. Extended / Core) to the Principal or Academic Coordinator before the entry deadline.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The Exams Officer Handbook says students choose 'with their teachers and coordinators' but gives the Head of Department no named step or date before entries close.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Curriculum Module: Exams Officer Handbook 26-27 (§5 Entries)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: Review predicted grades for your subject before they are submitted.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The School Principals Checklist has the Principal 'Review predicted grades with subject leaders', but the Subject Leader side has no timing or standard.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Curriculum Module: Assessment Policy 26-27 (§8.7 Predicted Grades)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: Check each year's Cambridge syllabus updates and Principal Examiner Reports and record the changes in the Scheme of Work.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The Principals Checklist gives this to the Principal 'with subject coordinators'; naming the Head of Department's part would make sure schemes of work actually change.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Curriculum Module: Implementation Toolkit 26-27 (July launch) or Department Handbook Template 26-27

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: Advise the Principal on an eligible same-subject mentor for each new teacher in the department.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: Mentor matching needs subject knowledge and the Principal assigns mentors; the Oversight Guide could name the Subject Leader's advisory part.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A monthly look at walkthrough coverage in the department (which teachers have had written walkthrough feedback in Edunav).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The handbook says walkthrough feedback 'must be shared with the teacher in writing through the school Edunav system', but nobody checks coverage; it would make SL2-004 more than a reminder.
